transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I’ve started to feel like I’m just not good enough at anything anymore, no matter how hard I try. It's just been really hard to shake this feeling lately, and my husband suggested I come speak with you.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for at least two weeks or longer?

It's been much longer than just a few weeks, to be honest. This heavy, constant feeling has been dragging me down for a little over two years now, starting right around when my husband and I began fertility treatments. It has just felt like a continuous, exhausting struggle that never really lifts.
Have you had any periods lasting several weeks or more during this time when you did *not* feel depressed or low?
No, I haven't had any real breaks from it at all. This heavy, low mood has been pretty much continuous over the last two years, without any relief lasting more than a few days at most.
Have there been times during this two-year period when your mood actually improved a bit in response to positive events, even if just temporarily?

Not really, no. Even when something objectively good happens at school or with my husband, that heavy, gray feeling in my chest doesn't lift. I usually just find myself going through the motions and pretending to be fine.
Even when you're with people you love or doing things you used to enjoy, do you feel little or no pleasure at all, most of the time?

I'm not entirely sure if it's a complete lack of pleasure, but I just feel so constantly drained, heavy, and sad. It makes it incredibly difficult to really engage or feel present even during those times.
Can you think of any activity, even something you once loved, that still brings you a brief sense of enjoyment or satisfaction, even if just for a moment?

I used to love painting and going to our Sunday family dinners, but now painting is just a distraction to keep my mind busy, and those dinners have become emotionally exhausting. Honestly, nothing really brings me genuine enjoyment anymore, and nothing lifts this heavy sadness, even for a moment.

The absence of mood reactivity to positive events, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, and persistent feelings of sadness and fatigue further support a persistent depressive presentation. No features of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or acute major depressive episode with full remission were reported, and the chronicity exceeds the duration required for recurrent depressive disorder. Therefore, the candidate list remains unchanged.
